speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You presented with persistent vomiting and chest pain; to begin our evaluation, please describe exactly when the pain started and if it radiates to your jaw, neck, or arm. Additionally, have you noticed any blood in your vomit or experienced shortness of breath?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave Syndrome (Mucosal rupture of the esophagus).

Given the history of forceful vomiting following heavy alcohol consumption, followed by choking, coughing, and chest pain, this clinical picture is highly suggestive of esophageal rupture. I will proceed with urgent imaging to confirm the diagnosis and assess for mediastinal air or fluid.
